dct_description_sm: Hydrological and sediment flux responses to climate change in small watersheds of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago have not been undertaken. Yet environmental change in the Arctic is expected to be amplified, since recent and near future increases in air temperature and precipitation will be among the largest on the planet.  These results are of interdisciplinary interest, and are globally and regionally important for (1) anticipating future landscape and fluvial change in cold environments, (2) assessing likely climatic controls contained in lacustrine and marine sedimentary archives influenced by nival rivers, (3) quantifying sediment budgets in cold regions and sediment delivery to lacustrine and marine basins (Beylich et al., 2009 and Syvitski, 2002), (4) comparing results with global runoff and sediment flux databases, which currently lack data from small High Arctic rivers (Milliman and Syvitski, 1992), and (5) anticipating future and current aquatic fluxes of carbon, nitrogen, and other nutrients (Lafrenire and Lamoureux, 2008), given that sediment and nutrient supplies are often closely linked (Schlnz and Schneider, 2000).
